solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Boat a metre in length

indicators.note: the short pair sits within the word for a length, as the clue's phrasing places it

parts.note: a span is a measure of length, from thumb to little finger
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small vessel described as no longer than a metre.
explanation.definitionFit: A sampan is a flat-bottomed skiff used in Chinese and South-East Asian harbours, so it is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Safety device testable when faulty

indicators.note: something faulty is not working properly, so the letters of testable are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A piece of protective equipment that can be checked whenever it goes wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat belt is the car harness that restrains a passenger in a crash, a classic piece of safety equipment.

clue.text: State with ocean on East

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece placed on another sits above it, so the ocean comes first

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea

explanation.surface: A US state lying beside the Atlantic on the country's eastern side.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is the north-easternmost of the United States, so it names one of the states.

clue.text: Effort in a racing event, almost exhausted

parts.note: taken as written
the TT (Tourist Trophy) is the motorcycle race held on the Isle of Man

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for exhausted is dropped

parts.note: a supply that is exhausted is empty

explanation.surface: A competitor makes a bid during a race while nearly worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the famous Isle of Man motorcycle race, a common crossword stand-in for any race.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt is a try or bid at doing something, which is what an effort can mean.

clue.text: Unconfirmed report is, accordingly, held back by doctor

indicators.note: held means kept inside, so the doctor's letters hold the reversed pair between them

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, the British family doctor

indicators.note: back means the two short words are read in reverse order and direction

parts.note: taken as written
so can mean therefore or accordingly

explanation.surface: A rumour is being withheld, so to speak, by a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: GP is the British term for a family doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossip is idle talk or rumour that has not been verified, exactly a report nobody has confirmed.

clue.text: Where you'll find isolated soldiers excel in sending dispatches?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a remote military station far from the main army
second meaning, whimsically: to beat someone at posting mail

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into OUT (surpass) plus POST (send mail), as in outrun or outdo; the question mark flags that invented verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpost is a small detached garrison stationed at a distance from the main force.

clue.text: Disorder resulted before start of match that's played by West Indians

indicators.note: the jumbled word comes before the next piece in the answer
used as a verb, to disorder the letters of resulted is to jumble them

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the opening letter of match is taken

parts.note: only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: Chaos broke out ahead of a cricket match involving the West Indies.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a West Indies cricket match, but the definition is an instrument played in the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: The steel drum, or steel pan, is the percussion instrument developed in Trinidad and played throughout the Caribbean.

clue.text: Satisfy professor, initially, with tenure

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of professor alone

parts.note: only its first letter is used
a lease is a tenure, the right to hold property for a term

explanation.surface: Keep an academic happy by first granting them a permanent post.
explanation.walkthrough: Tenure looks like the academic job-for-life, but here it is the property sense: a period of holding land or premises.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to give them satisfaction or gratify them.

clue.text: Cold wine returned in cylindrical container

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the Greek wine's letters are read from end to start

parts.note: retsina is a Greek resinated wine

explanation.surface: Chilled wine sent back to the cellar in a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a round metal container such as a tin for tea or film, typically cylindrical.

clue.text: Logical thinker helping with a nautical problem

parts.note: a ration is a portion or helping of food
taken as written
a ship that lists leans to one side, a list

explanation.surface: A clear-headed person lends a hand with a puzzle at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Helping reads as assisting, but it is the noun: a portion of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationalist bases opinions on reason rather than emotion or faith, a thinker who follows logic.

clue.text: Place for sea cruises linked to particular subject

wordplay.note: the Med, short for the Mediterranean, is a favourite cruising sea

explanation.surface: A cruise destination tied in with some special topic.
explanation.walkthrough: The Med is the everyday British name for the Mediterranean Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A themed event or collection is organised around one particular topic.

clue.text: Bishops taken in by a European cleric from France

indicators.note: the bishops are taken inside the pair of letters that follow

parts.note: taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Senior churchmen are fooled by a French priest.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken in by looks like being deceived; here it means being placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbé is the French title for an abbot or other ecclesiastic, so it names a French clergyman.

clue.text: Still not ready to start debate?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, whimsically: lacking a motion, the proposal a formal debate needs

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as motion-less: a debating society cannot begin until a motion is tabled.
explanation.definitionFit: Something motionless is perfectly still, with no movement at all.

clue.text: Extensive traveller's log possibly improved, without rubbish

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of log could be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the improved word goes round the rubbish

parts.note: something improved is better
rot is nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A seasoned traveller's journal, perhaps polished up with the junk removed.
explanation.walkthrough: Without looks like 'minus', but here it carries its old sense of 'outside', so one piece wraps round another. The 's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A globetrotter is someone who travels widely around the world, the very picture of an extensive traveller.

clue.text: Use bad language, with sheep, lamb going astray

indicators.note: animals going astray wander off, so the letters of both words are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A farmer curses as the ewes and the lamb wander off.
explanation.definitionFit: To blaspheme is to speak profanely about sacred things, to swear or curse.

clue.text: Fresh fish secured by pub ahead of time

indicators.note: the enclosed piece comes ahead of the final letter
the fish is held fast inside the pub, secured within its letters

parts.note: an inn is a pub
the sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: A newly caught fish is locked up in a pub ahead of schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Fresh suggests newly caught fish; here it means cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh in the informal sense means impudent or cheeky, which is what insolent means.

clue.text: Pressure to mark up people in fitting evaluation

indicators.note: the three pieces are placed in the word meaning fitting, which surrounds them

parts.note: something apt is suitable or fitting
to raise a price is to mark it up
men here stands for people in general

explanation.surface: Pressure to increase a mark in a staff appraisal that feels fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Appraisement is an older term for appraisal, the formal assessment of something's value or worth.

clue.text: Drama ultimately penned by British playwright for producer of picture

indicators.note: penned means shut in, so the playwright's name encloses the letter

parts.note: Harold Pinter was a British dramatist, author of The Birthday Party

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of drama

parts.note: only its last letter is used

explanation.surface: A play finally written by a British dramatist gives rise to a film.
explanation.walkthrough: Penned looks like 'written', apt next to a playwright, but it means enclosed. Picture suggests a film; here it is a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter makes paintings, so is the artist who produces a picture.

clue.text: Do division in maths, e.g. mentally

indicators.note: in points to letters sitting inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the answer lies across the end of one word, all of the next and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Work out a division sum in your head, as in mental arithmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: Division looks like the arithmetic operation, but the definition wants the verb: to cut something into parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To segment something is to split it into sections, which is performing a division of it.

clue.text: Unexpected result that may come at end of either leg

definitions.text: that may come at end of either leg
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the folded cuff at the bottom of a trouser leg

explanation.walkthrough: Leg suggests a stage of a two-legged football tie, where a surprise result fits; the second sense is tailoring. A turn-up is British for a trouser cuff.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a turn-up is both a surprising development and the folded-back hem of trousers.

clue.text: Ring-leader captured in small revolt — that's unexpected

indicators.note: the leader's letter is captured inside the other pieces, enclosed by them

parts.note: an uprising is a revolt

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: The ringleader of a minor rebellion has been caught, which nobody saw coming.
explanation.walkthrough: Ring-leader looks like one word for an instigator; split, it gives the first letter of ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Something surprising is something you did not expect, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Bear ridicule, when it's repeated

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Winnie-the-..., A. A. Milne's bear
second meaning: said twice, the word gives ...-..., to dismiss with scorn

explanation.walkthrough: Bear looks like a verb (put up with); it is the noun, a famous fictional bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooh is the bear of Milne's children's stories, and doubling the word gives a verb for scoffing at something.

clue.text: Run into parents in European city

indicators.note: the run is placed into the middle of the parents' letters

parts.note: pa and ma are informal words for father and mother
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Bumping into your mother and father on holiday in a continental city.
explanation.walkthrough: Run into suggests a chance meeting; here 'into' alone signals insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Parma is a city in northern Italy, famous for its ham and cheese.

clue.text: Be a consumer? Not seriously, from what we hear

indicators.note: from what we hear means judging by sound, so the phrase is spoken and respelt

parts.note: something said in jest is not meant seriously

explanation.surface: Asking whether one is a shopper, said only half seriously as far as anyone can tell.
explanation.walkthrough: Consumer reads as a shopper; the question mark flags the literal sense of one who takes food in.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest is to take food or drink into the body, the most literal way of consuming.

clue.text: Male getting into right group for speculations

indicators.note: the male gets into the group's letters, placed inside them

parts.note: the Tories are the British Conservative Party, on the political right
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man joins a right-wing party in a scheme of guesses.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tories are Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Theories are proposed explanations not yet proven, which is what speculations are.

clue.text: Effort by author of short stories who also wrote this

indicators.note: by means beside, and the effort sits right beside the author's name, after it

parts.words: author of short stories who also wrote
parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe wrote short stories such as The Tell-Tale Heart and poems like The Raven
a try is an effort or attempt

explanation.surface: An attempt by a short-story writer who also turned his hand to verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the single word this, pointing back at the answer: Poe also wrote poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Poe was famous for poems such as The Raven, so verse is the other kind of writing the clue points to.

clue.text: One of several monarchs providing university in beginning

indicators.note: the university's letter is set in the word for beginning

parts.note: a start is a beginning

explanation.surface: A king who funded a university at the start of his reign.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stuarts were the royal house of Scotland and later England from James I to Queen Anne.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuart is the family name shared by a line of Scottish and English kings and queens, so it names any one of them.
